leftEvidence.title: David’s oath and God’s oath meet at Zion

points.label: Action and response
points.left: The song recalls David’s search for a dwelling, calls the ark to rest, asks for the anointed, quotes the oath about offspring, and names Zion’s choice, provision, priesthood, horn, and crown.
points.right: The speaker blesses God for training, asks what humanity is, seeks rescue from foreign mouths, promises a new song, and imagines sons, daughters, barns, flocks, and secure streets.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places human resolve to find a dwelling stands beside divine oath and choice inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places warrior dependence and communal abundance share one prayer inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Psalms 132:1–18 and Psalms 144:1–15 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: A David prayer joins warfare, frailty, rescue, and flourishing

payload.tension: Psalms 132:1–18 foregrounds human resolve to find a dwelling stands beside divine oath and choice; Psalms 144:1–15 foregrounds warrior dependence and communal abundance share one prayer. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
